claims.text: All cause renal toxicity (often reversible), vestibular/auditory toxicity (often irreversible; vertigo, ataxia) and prolonged neuromuscular blockade
claims.quote: All aminoglycosides cause - Renal toxicity (often reversible) - Vestibular and auditory toxicity (often irreversible) - Prolongation of effects of neuromuscular blockers Symptoms and signs of vestibular damage are vertigo and ataxia.

Aminoglycosides can prolong the effect of neuromuscular blockers (eg, succinylcholine, curare-like drugs) and worsen weakness in disorders affecting neuromuscular transmission (eg, myasthenia gravis).

claims.text: Risk rises with high or frequent doses, high levels, >3 days, older age, renal disease, other nephrotoxins (eg, vancomycin, contrast); loop diuretics add ototoxicity.
claims.quote: Risk factors for renal, vestibular, and auditory toxicity are - Frequent or very high doses - Very high blood levels of the drug - Long duration of therapy (particularly > 3 days) - Older age - A preexisting renal disorder - Coadministration of vancomycin, cyclosporine, amphotericin B, iodinated contrast agents, or other nephrotoxins - For auditory toxicity, a genetic predisposition, preexisting hearing problems, and coadministration of loop diuretics
Aminoglycosides are contraindicated in patients who are allergic to them.

claims.text: Pregnancy: possible fetal risk (eg, auditory toxicity with streptomycin), but benefit may outweigh it.
claims.quote: With aminoglycosides, there may be risk to the fetus (eg, auditory toxicity with streptomycin), but clinical benefits may outweigh risk.
claims.locator: Use of Aminoglycosides During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding
